title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding and Decoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel information encoding and decoding scheme leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core concept involves utilizing multi-particle entangled states for superposition-based encoding and subsequent information recovery through measurement outcomes. Furthermore, the scheme incorporates entanglement-assisted eavesdropping detection and error correction mechanisms. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential to surpass the classical channel capacity limit, fundamentally altering the landscape of information transmission. The proposed approach explores the physical boundaries of information transfer, offering a new pathway for quantum communication protocols. The key mathematical elements underpinning the system are presented, including the quantum state description, measurement operators, and the relevant equations governing the process. The system's performance is evaluated through theoretical modeling, highlighting its advantages in terms of information rate and security.

title: Causal Discovery from Streaming Data with Bayesian Gaussian Processes
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal discovery using Bayesian Gaussian Processes (BGPs) specifically designed for streaming data. Traditional causal discovery methods often struggle with the continuous arrival of new data, necessitating either computationally expensive batch processing or simplified models that fail to capture temporal dependencies. This work addresses these limitations by developing an iterative algorithm that learns a BGP model from a stream of observations. The algorithm incorporates prior beliefs about causal relationships and dynamically updates the model with each incoming observation, effectively handling temporal dynamics and quantifying uncertainty. The core of the approach lies in leveraging the representational power of BGP to model complex, non-linear relationships while maintaining probabilistic inference. The proposed method offers a robust framework for causal discovery in scenarios where data arrives continuously, providing a principled way to infer causal connections and their associated uncertainties. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through the theoretical analysis and the outlining of the key algorithmic components. This work contributes to the growing field of causal discovery by providing a practical and scalable solution for analyzing streaming data.

title: Continuous Learning Framework Based on Memory Retrieval
abstract: This paper proposes a novel continuous learning framework centered around memory retrieval. The core idea is to leverage a memory bank to facilitate continual learning, aiming to enhance both the generalization ability and the continuous learning capabilities of the model. The framework operates by continuously learning new data while periodically retrieving and re-training on data stored within this memory bank. This approach addresses limitations of existing continuous learning methods which often rely solely on online or offline learning strategies. The key mechanism involves the random selection of data from the memory bank during the training of new data, effectively boosting learning efficiency and improving generalization performance. We present a detailed description of the framework, including the architecture, memory management strategy, and the retrieval process. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and discuss future research directions.

title: Quantum Chaos Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Chaos Optimization Algorithm (QCOA) is a novel optimization algorithm inspired by quantum chaos theory, designed to automatically discover optimal solutions for complex systems. This algorithm leverages the inherent properties of quantum chaos, specifically its self-alignment and stochastic nature, to efficiently navigate intricate problem spaces and identify optimal configurations. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adjusted quantum state representation, enabling the algorithm to explore a vast solution space with enhanced adaptability and reduced computational cost compared to traditional optimization techniques. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant potential across diverse fields, including machine learning, circuit design, and materials science, offering a fundamentally new approach to problem-solving. This paper will detail the theoretical underpinnings of the QCOA, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in challenging scenarios.

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamic Topology Transformation
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for quantum state transformation leveraging quantum entanglement. Traditional approaches often rely on computationally intensive algorithms, while this method utilizes entanglement to enable adaptive transformations of quantum states, thereby enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of quantum algorithms. We explore the fundamental principles behind this approach, detailing the core mechanism and highlighting the advantages over existing techniques. The paper introduces a unique framework for dynamically adjusting quantum states based on entanglement, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize quantum computing.

title: Title: Fractal Constraint Optimization (FCO) for Algorithmic Diversity
abstract: Fractal Constraint Optimization (FCO) presents a novel approach to optimization, integrating fractal geometry with constraint satisfaction to unlock solutions to complex problems previously intractable through classical methods. This paper explores the design and implementation of a hybrid algorithm that leverages fractal representations of the search space to generate diverse solutions, guided by constraint satisfaction to guarantee optimal performance. The core mechanism involves constructing fractal landscapes, dynamically adjusting constraints, and iteratively refining solutions through a feedback loop. We demonstrate the effectiveness of FCO in solving a range of optimization challenges, showcasing its potential to facilitate creative problem-solving and overcome limitations of traditional optimization techniques.

title: Research on seedling grading of Platycladus orientalis based on fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm improved by genetic sparrow family search optimization
abstract: Platycladus orientalis has high ecological and economic value, but the quality of Platycladus orientalis seedlings varies greatly. The original quality grading standard is relatively simple and the grading boundary is not clear. It is of great significance to use the in-situ Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) technique for nondestructive testing of Platycladus orientalis roots and the improved fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm for scientific and accurate grading of Platycladus orientalis seedlings combined with morphological parameters.As a result, five parameters were found reflecting the quality of Platycladus orientalis seedlings, including phase angle at 4000Hz and tangent value at 400kHz, which could reflect the quality of roots. An Fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering algorithm improved by genetic sparrow family search optimization (GSFS-FCM) was proposed. Through the test of standard functions and typical datasets, it was found that the number of clusters of the algorithm could be determined automatically. Although the running time is increased, the number of iterations is reduced by more than 12%, and the clustering error rate is reduced by more than 8%. Finally, eight months old Platycladus orientalis seedlings were divided into six grades with the GSFS-FCM algorithm.From the present study it can be concluded that among the Platycladus orientalis seedlings root EIS parameters measured by the instrument in situ, phase angle at 4000Hz and tangent value at 400kHz can be used to represent the quality of the roots. GSFS-FCM algorithm can effectively and automatically grading the seedlings of Platycladus orientalis without specifying the number of clusters. The algorithm has fewer iterations and higher accuracy.

title: Intelligent Recommendation for Safety Risk Precontrol Knowledge in Mega Hydropower Engineering Construction: A Hybrid Method Driven by Textual Semantics
abstract: Abstract Mega hydropower engineering (MHE) is mostly located in complex areas with high mountains and deep valleys. The construction environment is harsh, the operating space is limited, and the work processes are highly coupled, resulting in a high incidence of various safety risks and difficulty in precontrol. The formulation of traditional risk precontrol measures primarily relies on manual consultation of safety management standards, which is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to errors. This approach struggles to meet the modern engineering requirements for real-time performance and accuracy. Furthermore, existing research has largely concentrated on postaccident investigation and response, without sufficiently leveraging the value of construction safety knowledge, such as safety management standards and historical precontrol measures, to establish a proactive risk prevention system. To fill this gap, this study first analyzes the data characteristics of construction safety knowledge and extracts its semantic features using the contrastive sentence embedding (CSE) method and general language model (GLM). A multiscale text semantic feature fusion network based on an interactive attention mechanism is developed to realize the interactive fusion of semantic features. Second, a text semantic deep matching model, CSGLM-TSDM, was constructed based on this network to quantify the semantic similarity between each safety risk factor and its precontrol knowledge. Finally, an intelligent recommendation method based on semantic similarity is developed using knowledge retrieval and inference techniques. This method can recommend the precontrol knowledge and score corresponding to each safety risk factor in real time. The results show that (1) the F1-score of the CSGLM-TSDM semantic matching model on the self-built data set is 97.57%, and the model performance is superior, and (2) the intelligent recommendation method can quickly reason out the top n precontrol knowledge and their scores with the highest similarity to any safety risk factor. The method’s average precision for recalling the top 10 pieces of knowledge reached 98.95%. This study provides a reusable computational framework for building a proactive safety prevention and control system in the global hydropower and large-scale infrastructure construction sectors. It offers significant value as a reference for the intelligent transformation of knowledge-driven engineering safety management.

title: One-Shot and Concurrent Hitting Times for Grover-Coined Quantum Walks on Cubelike Graphs
abstract: We study the one-shot and concurrent hitting for the discrete-time Grover-coined quantum walk on cubelike graphs $G=\text{Cay}(\mathbb Z_2^d,Ω)$ of degree $Δ=|Ω|$. Starting from the vertex labeled $0$, we identify $σ=\bigoplus_{ω\inΩ}ω$ as a natural target vertex; for the hypercube, $σ$ is precisely the antipodal vertex. For families with $Δ\to\infty$, let $T$ be an integer having the same parity as $Δ$ and satisfying $ \left|T-\frac{πΔ}{2}\right|\leq 1. $ We show that the probability $p_T(σ)$ of finding the walker at $σ$ when it is measured at time $T$ satisfies $$ p_T(σ)=1-O(Δ^{-1/5}). $$ Thus the target is found with probability tending to one after $Θ(Δ)$ steps. For the concurrently measured walk, let $H_T^{\mathrm{Conc}}(σ)$ denote the probability that the target is detected at or before time $T$ when it is tested after every step. We prove $$ p_T(σ)\leq T H_T^{\mathrm{Conc}}(σ), $$ which implies $H_T^{\mathrm{Conc}}(σ)=Ω(Δ^{-1})$ over the same time scale. The proof uses the Walsh-Fourier decomposition, an exact two-dimensional reduction of each Fourier mode, and a universal second-moment identity for the associated character sums. Our results extend Kempe's hypercube hitting phenomenon (J. Kempe, Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 133, 215-235, 2005) to arbitrary cubelike generating sets and establish the conjectured asymptotic hitting behavior for cublelike and augmented cubes in Mulherkar, Rajdeepak and Sunitha (Int. J. Quantum Inf. 20,2250020, 2022)

title: VERGE: Verification-Enhanced Refinement for Grounded Extraction of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Symptoms in Clinical Notes
abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer is increasing among younger adults, yet red-flag symptoms in this age group have no evidence-based guidelines for follow-up testing, and structured encounter data do not capture the detail needed to support early detection and inform follow-up, including symptom duration, context, and fam- ily history, an established colorectal-cancer risk factor. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an automated method for extracting six red-flag symptoms and family-history risk status from free-text clinical notes. We developed VERGE, an agentic workflow in which an initial label and evidence are proposed using retrieval-augmented generation, then passed through a bounded verification- refinement cycle that checks textual grounding and clinical validity, corrects and rechecks a claim until resolved or a limit is reached, and escalates unresolved claims for human review. VERGE was evaluated on 4,033 clinician-labeled note-finding pairs against a single-agent baseline, a rule-based clinical language-processing baseline, and an alternative underlying language model. Compared with the single-agent baseline, VERGE reduced false positive find- ings, improving precision from 0.764 to 0.849 and MCC from 0.681 to 0.730, a balanced gain across the precision-recall trade-off, and resolved most flagged errors autonomously, with human review required for only 1.5 percent of claims. These results indicate that a bounded, verification-based workflow can reduce unnecessary positive findings without sacrificing the ability to detect true ones. This approach offers a path toward more reliable and trustworthy clinical language-processing tools to support colorectal cancer risk assessment in younger patients.

title: DropClick: Semi-Automated One-Click Segmentation for Agricultural Robotic Data
abstract: Labelling vision datasets, especially for segmentation tasks, is a laborious and costly process that stymies novel developments in agricultural robotics. In this paper, we present DropClick, a click-guided segmentation tool that simplifies the annotation process. Our system utilises single-click inputs on objects to generate pseudo-labels, which can replace manual annotations. DropClick stands out as it is a semi-automated approach and does not require a click for every object in the scene. It can therefore further reduce the required amount of user input drastically. We evaluate our method on two challenging agricultural robotic datasets, SB20 and BUP20 for plant and fruit segmentation, respectively. DropClick is first trained on a small subset of just 5 images from the original training data. This DropClick model can then be deployed as a one-click segmentation system and achieves comparable or higher performance than other one-click methods achieving an mIoU of 70.0 and 72.6 points, for SB20 and BUP20 respectively. DropClick then excels at maintaining high performance when clicks are not given (e.g. dropped); when 50% of the clicks are missing it still maintains an mIoU of 68.9 and 71.3 points, for SB20 and BUP20 respectively. We validate DropClick as a pseudo-labelling approach by taking its outputs to train a Mask2Former instance-based segmentation model in a semi-supervised manner. In this process, partially removing user input from DropClick yields similar high performance when compared to providing all clicks, at 70.1 vs 70.7 points AP50 for SB20 and no difference for BUP20 at 77.0 for both models; at the same time saving 46.3% of total input for SB20 and 31.9% for BUP20.

title: FLY-EVAL++: An Evidence-Driven Evaluation Protocol for Safety-Constrained Flight Prediction with Large Language Models
abstract: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) in safety-critical, physics-governed environments requires more than accuracy-based metrics, because predictions that are numerically close to the ground truth can still violate operational constraints, combine fields in physically inconsistent ways, or fail to produce usable structured outputs. Existing evaluation protocols do not measure these failure modes reliably. We propose FLY-EVAL++, an evidence-driven evaluation protocol that combines deterministic verification of protocol compliance, physical feasibility, and safety constraints with fixed rubric-guided aggregation into interpretable multi-dimensional scores. We instantiate FLY-EVAL++ for Flight Trajectory and Attitude Prediction (FTAP) by extending the PilotBench setting with history-conditioned and multi-step prediction tasks. Across 66 LLMs, safety compliance is the most discriminative dimension of model behavior: models with comparable predictive performance differ by more than 28 points in safety score, and we observe recurrent failures including safety violations under physically plausible predictions and instability in multi-step rollouts. These results show that evaluation in safety-critical domains should measure constraint satisfaction and structured validity explicitly rather than rely on accuracy-centric reporting alone.

We propose FLY-EVAL++, an evidence-driven evaluation protocol that combines deterministic verification of protocol compliance, physical feasibility, and safety constraints with fixed rubric-guided aggregation into interpretable multi-dimensional scores. We instantiate FLY-EVAL++ for Flight Trajectory and Attitude Prediction (FTAP) by extending the PilotBench setting with history-conditioned and multi-step prediction tasks. Across 66 LLMs, safety compliance is the most discriminative dimension of model behavior: models with comparable predictive performance differ by more than 28 points in safety score, and we observe recurrent failures including safety violations under physically plausible predictions and instability in multi-step rollouts. These results show that evaluation in safety-critical domains should measure constraint satisfaction and structured validity explicitly rather than rely on accuracy-centric reporting alone.

title: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to edit existing code, but correctness alone is not enough: useful repairs should also be minimal, reviewable, and faithful to the original implementation. We study over-editing, the tendency of a model to rewrite code beyond what is required to fix a bug. We construct an evaluation framework from 400 BigCodeBench problems by injecting controlled AST-level corruptions into reference solutions, giving each repair task a known minimal patch. Across frontier LLMs, over-editing is widespread even among strong models like GPT-5.5: high Pass@1 can coexist with unnecessarily large edits and added cognitive complexity. A preservation instruction substantially reduces this behavior, lowering average excess Levenshtein distance from 0.195 to 0.131, reducing added cognitive complexity by 26.6%, and increasing Pass@1 by 2.3 points. However, these gains do not simply follow from a larger reasoning budget or larger models. We next ask whether minimal editing can be learned directly during post-training. We observe that supervised fine-tuning overfits to seen corruption patterns, whereas reinforcement learning gives the best out-of-domain edit-fidelity and performance-retention trade-off. These results position edit fidelity as a distinct axis of code-repair quality and show that it can be measured and learned.

title: SVG-Score: Human-Aligned Evaluation of Text-to-SVG Generation
abstract: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) generation is attracting increasing attention as generative models improve in expressiveness and controllability. Progress, however, is held back by the lack of domain-specific evaluation protocols: current practice relies on metrics designed for natural images, most notably CLIPScore, which was never trained on vector graphics and aligns only partially with human judgment. We introduce \textbf{\ours}, a human-aligned evaluation framework for text-to-SVG generation. Through controlled caption and image perturbations, we first show that CLIP-based scores barely react to the errors SVG generators actually make, such as wrong colors, counts, and spatial relations, and that off-the-shelf Vision-Language Model (VLM) judges, while more sensitive, respond unevenly across error types and SVG styles. We then introduce a human-annotated dataset for \textit{Semantic Alignment}, measuring how faithfully a generated SVG reflects its caption. Building on it, we develop two complementary evaluators: CLIP scorers adapted to vector graphics and then aligned to human preferences, for fast large-scale evaluation, and a VLM judge trained with supervised fine-tuning and reward-shaped reinforcement learning, for more expressive and interpretable assessment. Using both, we benchmark major open-source, commercial, and optimization-based SVG generators on an independent caption set.

title: Client-Side Probing of Deleted Ridge Statistics in Federated Unlearning
abstract: Federated unlearning aims to remove a client's data from a shared model without retraining from scratch. Some efficient systems make deletion exact by storing compact, additive summaries of the training features and broadcasting an updated linear classifier after every accepted change. We show that these broadcasts can also reveal the hidden summaries. A malicious client can submit known changes, use the returned classifiers to identify the server state, and compare states immediately before and after an isolated deletion. This exposes the deleted sample, class, or client summary and can enable its reinsertion. We characterize exactly when the observations contain enough independent information, give a matching optimal construction for unrestricted probes, and derive a more realistic estimator based on additions formed from the attacker's own data. On MNIST and CIFAR-10, high-precision broadcasts permit exact label recovery for every tested sample deletion with both probe types. Lower-precision broadcasts sharply reduce fine-grained recovery, and insufficiently diverse responses prevent identification altogether. Unrestricted probes are readily detected by their size; most individual attacker-data additions resemble honest batches, although we do not claim that the complete sequence is inconspicuous. The results identify a concrete privacy and integrity risk, its algebraic cause, and practical limits involving broadcast precision, update verification, response rate, and concurrent activity.

title: Nature-Inspired Algorithms in Data Analytics: A Unified Cross Domain Benchmarking Framework
abstract: The rapid growth of high-dimensional and heterogeneous datasets has intensified the demand for scalable and robust optimization approaches in data analytics. Traditional deterministic algorithms frequently suffer from premature convergence, initialization sensitivity, and reduced performance in nonlinear or noisy environments. Nature-inspired algorithms (NIAs), including evolutionary, swarm-based, and physics-inspired approaches, provide stochastic population based mechanisms capable of navigating complex search spaces effectively. This study develops a unified cross-domain benchmarking framework for evaluating NIAs across feature selection, clustering, predictive modeling, and image segmentation tasks. A structured taxonomy is introduced, and performance is analyzed along five dimensions: predictive accuracy, convergence efficiency, computational complexity, robustness, and hybridization trade-offs. Mathematical formulations of representative algorithms (Genetic Algorithms, Particle Swarm Optimization, Ant Colony Optimization, Simulated Annealing) are incorporated to strengthen analytical rigor. Comparative synthesis reveals that algorithm suitability is task-dependent: evolutionary algorithms excel in feature selection, swarm-based approaches converge efficiently in clustering, and hybrid models yield superior predictive performance at increased computational cost. The proposed framework establishes standardized evaluation criteria to enhance reproducibility and cross-domain comparability. The findings provide theoretical insight and practical guidance for selecting nature-inspired optimization strategies in complex data-driven environments.

title: 基于量子纠缠的概率论验证与扩展
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic framework rooted in quantum entanglement, offering a robust and potentially transformative approach to quantum computing verification and broader probabilistic prediction. Traditional probabilistic methods often rely on approximations and assumptions. We introduce a quantum-enhanced probability calculation model predicated on entanglement, aiming to surpass these limitations through enhanced accuracy and the potential for more profound probabilistic insights. The core mechanism involves utilizing entanglement to dynamically adjust the probability distribution, allowing for more precise and nuanced predictions compared to classical approaches. We explore the framework's capabilities through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulation, highlighting its potential to refine existing probability models and open new avenues in uncertainty quantification.

title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Optimization Strategies
abstract: Quantum algorithm optimization is a challenging task, requiring sophisticated strategies to maximize algorithm performance. This paper introduces a novel optimization approach utilizing dynamic data and hardware characteristics to automatically adjust quantum algorithm parameters and steps. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic data structure that adapts to the quantum algorithm's current state and hardware properties, resulting in enhanced efficiency. We present a theoretical framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this method through a rigorous analysis of specific quantum algorithms. The research highlights the significant benefits of this dynamic optimization strategy compared to traditional static approaches.

title: Dynamic Geometry Transformation Optimization via Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing to optimize dynamic geometric transformations. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexity of these transformations, limiting processing speed and precision. We propose a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum algorithms to accelerate the computation of these transformations. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum superposition and entanglement to represent and manipulate geometric states in a fundamentally different manner than classical approaches. This allows for the potential for significantly faster and more accurate transformations, opening new avenues for advancements in fields such as computer graphics, image processing, and scientific modeling. The presented work demonstrates the feasibility of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Field Theory for Quantum Information Security
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear geometric field theory (NLGFT) as a foundation for quantum information security. We propose a novel protocol leveraging the inherent properties of geometric fields to safeguard information, offering enhanced resilience against various attacks. The core mechanism centers on encoding information within geometric structures, exploiting their dynamic and complex properties to create a robust security system. This approach distinguishes itself from traditional cryptographic methods by focusing on the spatial distribution of information, providing a fundamentally new paradigm for quantum information protection. We detail the design of a protocol incorporating key elements of NLGFT, including the representation of information as geometric primitives, the application of entanglement to enhance security, and the use of geometric transformations to mitigate potential vulnerabilities. The potential implications of this research extend to the development of more secure and adaptable quantum cryptographic systems.

title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos – A Computational Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel computational framework for Bayesian Geometric Chaos, a system of interest where the evolution of a geometric system is governed by probabilistic equations. We propose a Bayesian approach to model and predict the evolution of such systems, incorporating uncertainty quantification directly into the model's dynamics. The framework leverages a probabilistic model to represent the system's state and evolution, allowing for adaptive uncertainty representation and prediction. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulations, illustrating its ability to capture complex emergent behaviors within chaotic systems. The core mechanism focuses on creating a probabilistic model, enabling dynamic uncertainty representation and prediction.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Chaos Information Adaptive Algorithm (CIS), designed to address optimization challenges within complex systems. The core mechanism centers around the introduction of a "Chaos Information" adaptive adjustment strategy, which exploits the self-adaptive nature of chaotic systems to achieve a more robust and efficient optimization process. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the CIS algorithm, including its theoretical foundation, implementation details, and experimental validation, demonstrating its efficacy in optimizing various systems.

title: Adaptive Recurrent Neural Networks: A Dynamic Gradient Descent Strategy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic gradient descent strategy based on adaptive recurrent neural networks (ARNs). The core challenge in training deep learning models is often the need to efficiently adapt to evolving data distributions. Traditional gradient descent methods typically employ fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively handle data fluctuations. Our proposed approach leverages the inherent dynamics of ARNs to dynamically adjust the learning rate and step size during gradient descent, resulting in improved training speed, enhanced generalization performance, and a more robust model. The methodology is designed to automatically learn and utilize local features from the input data, minimizing the reliance on manually engineered features and promoting a more intuitive and adaptable learning process. We present a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of this dynamic gradient descent strategy across a range of datasets and model architectures.

title: Quantum Decoherence-Based Privacy-Preserving Distributed Computing (QDPC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to privacy-preserving distributed computing leveraging the principles of quantum decoherence. The core idea revolves around utilizing quantum decoherence to mask intermediate computation steps, thereby protecting the confidentiality of the data and results. We propose a distributed computing scheme that combines Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) with quantum decoherence protocols. Specifically, we introduce a method for encoding data and computation steps into quantum states, followed by a decoherence process designed to erase traces of these states after the desired calculation is completed. The scheme employs QKD for secure key exchange, which is then used to control the decoherence process and verify the integrity of the final result. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm for privacy protection, relying on the inherent unpredictability of quantum systems rather than computational complexity assumptions. We analyze the security and performance of the proposed QDPC scheme, demonstrating its potential for secure distributed computation in scenarios where traditional cryptographic methods may be vulnerable due to advances in computing power. The key contributions lie in the innovative application of quantum decoherence for data masking and the integration with QKD for secure control and verification.

title: Temporal Kernel Methods for Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Time series anomaly detection is a critical task across numerous domains, including finance, healthcare, and industrial monitoring. Traditional kernel methods, while powerful in general machine learning, often fall short when applied to time series data due to their inability to effectively model the inherent temporal dependencies present. This paper introduces a novel approach – Temporal Kernel Methods – specifically designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to develop a specialized kernel function that explicitly incorporates temporal lags and recurrence patterns within the time series. This allows the method to capture complex temporal relationships, leading to improved anomaly detection performance. We define a new kernel function, *K(s1, s2 | lag)*, which measures the similarity between two time series segments *s1* and *s2* considering a specified lag *lag*. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of its implementation. The resulting method provides a significant advancement in kernel methods for time series anomaly detection, offering a robust and accurate solution for identifying deviations from expected patterns. The key innovation lies in the tailored design of the kernel function, enabling a more nuanced understanding of temporal dependencies compared to generic kernel methods. This work lays a foundation for further research and development in this area.

We define a new kernel function, *K(s1, s2 | lag)*, which measures the similarity between two time series segments *s1* and *s2* considering a specified lag *lag*. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of its implementation. The resulting method provides a significant advancement in kernel methods for time series anomaly detection, offering a robust and accurate solution for identifying deviations from expected patterns. The key innovation lies in the tailored design of the kernel function, enabling a more nuanced understanding of temporal dependencies compared to generic kernel methods. This work lays a foundation for further research and development in this area.

title: 基于深度学习的量子控制优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum control optimization utilizing deep learning techniques. Traditional quantum control optimization methods often rely on complex analytical calculations or computationally intensive numerical simulations, limiting their applicability to complex quantum systems. This work proposes a framework where a deep learning model is trained to directly learn optimal control pulses for a given quantum system. The model, trained on simulated quantum dynamics, effectively learns the mapping between system states and control parameters. This automated approach offers the potential to significantly accelerate the process of quantum control design and potentially enable control of systems beyond the reach of conventional optimization methods. The core claim of this work is the automation of quantum control through deep learning. The central mechanism involves the construction of a deep learning model to simulate quantum behavior and learn optimal control pulses. The resulting system demonstrates a promising path towards efficient and adaptive quantum control.

title: Dynamic Semantic Dependency Network Generation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing natural language understanding and reasoning by generating a dynamic semantic dependency network. The core idea is to leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to create a network capable of continuously learning and adapting to complex semantic relationships within a system. Unlike traditional methods relying on static knowledge graphs or predefined rules, our system employs an iterative process of monitoring model performance across various tasks and adjusting the network's structure based on observed successes and failures. Specifically, we utilize a reward-based policy gradient RL algorithm to optimize the weights and connections within the network, effectively creating a dynamic representation of semantic dependencies. The resulting system demonstrates a significant improvement in understanding and reasoning capabilities compared to static approaches. The key contributions of this work include the development of a dynamic network architecture and the integration of RL for adaptive semantic relationship learning.

title: Adaptive Neuron Topology Network
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Neuron Topology Network (ANTN), a novel neural network architecture designed to enhance learning efficiency and generalization capability by dynamically adapting its topology. The core claim of this work is that the topology of a neural network can be adapted to input data, leading to improved learning and generalization. The proposed mechanism involves a dynamic neuron connection rule that allows for the adaptive increase or decrease of connections between neurons, guided by topological information and facilitating information transfer. ANTN mimics the learning mechanisms of biological neural systems through its dynamic topology. The network's architecture is defined by a set of interconnected neurons, each possessing a state (si) and an activation function (fi(si)). The key element is the connection matrix (W), which represents the strength of connections between neurons. This matrix is not fixed but evolves during the learning process. The update rule for the connection matrix is defined as: Wij(t+1) = Wij(t) * (1 + α * η * Hij(t)) where: * Wij(t) is the connection weight between neuron *i* and neuron *j* at time *t*. * α is the learning rate. * η is a scaling factor. * Hij(t) is a heuristic function that indicates the relevance of the connection between neurons *i* and *j* based on their states and the overall network topology. The heuristic function Hij(t) is defined as: Hij(t) = ∑k=1K gik(si(t)) * gjk(sj(t)) where: * gik(si(t)) is the activation function of neuron *i* at time *t*. * K is the number of neurons in the network. The network's output is calculated as the weighted sum of the neuron states: y(t) = ∑i=1K Wij(t) * si(t) The goal of the ANTN is to optimize the connection matrix (W) to minimize a defined loss function (L(W)), typically using gradient-based optimization methods. The adaptive topology is crucial for handling complex and high-dimensional data, allowing the network to focus on the most relevant connections and avoid overfitting. This approach offers a flexible and potentially more efficient alternative to traditional fixed-topology neural networks.

title: Meta-Learning for Automated Algorithm Design in Scientific Computing
abstract: This paper explores the application of meta-learning techniques to the automated design of numerical algorithms within the domain of scientific computing. The core idea is to train a meta-learner on a diverse dataset of existing numerical algorithms, enabling it to generalize and generate new algorithms tailored to specific problem characteristics. We present a framework for this approach, outlining the key components and potential benefits. The research demonstrates the feasibility of automating algorithm design, which could lead to the discovery of more efficient and potentially novel solutions for complex scientific computing problems. The primary focus is on the theoretical underpinnings and potential of this methodology, without requiring empirical experimentation. The proposed system leverages learned patterns from existing algorithms to create new ones, significantly reducing the reliance on human expertise in algorithm selection and design. This work highlights a shift towards intelligent algorithm design, paving the way for accelerated scientific discovery.

This allows for a more nuanced and accurate representation of quantum phenomena than static approaches. The proposed framework offers a significant step toward enhanced quantum simulation capabilities, particularly in systems exhibiting complex geometric constraints.

title: Dynamic Matrix Learning with Adaptive Feedback
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic matrix learning framework, termed Dynamic Matrix Learning with Adaptive Feedback, designed to address the limitations of traditional matrix learning methods in the face of dynamic data. The core principle of this framework is the automated adjustment of matrix parameters based on the input data's evolution, achieved through a feedback mechanism that promotes model adaptability. We detail the design of the dynamic matrix learning algorithm, the adaptive feedback loop, and the resulting improvements in learning efficiency and generalization ability. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in a variety of scenarios, showcasing its potential to overcome the constraints of static models and enhance performance in dynamic data analysis.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Quantum Topology Reconstruction
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating area of quantum physics, exhibits remarkable properties and potential applications across diverse fields, including quantum information processing and quantum cryptography. A significant challenge lies in the creation and manipulation of complex quantum states, particularly in the context of quantum geometry. This paper explores the design of an adaptive self-organizing quantum topology algorithm, aiming to dynamically adjust quantum topology structures based on input data, enabling high-precision reconstruction. The core mechanism leverages the inherent self-organizing capabilities of quantum topology to achieve this adaptability. We present a novel algorithm that incorporates feedback loops and iterative refinement to optimize the generated topology, offering a significant advancement over traditional approaches. The research highlights the potential of this algorithm to overcome limitations in achieving precise and robust quantum topology reconstruction, thereby opening up new avenues for research and applications.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive neural network parameter adjustment strategy designed to automatically optimize model performance and adapt to evolving data patterns. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often struggle to maintain optimal performance as data shifts, leading to suboptimal results. This work proposes a mechanism that iteratively adjusts network parameters based on a feedback loop incorporating both model performance metrics and data distribution shifts. The core of the approach involves a dynamic weighting scheme that prioritizes both accuracy and robustness, ensuring the network remains effectively tuned to the current data landscape. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy through a series of experiments evaluating its performance across various datasets and model architectures. The results showcase a significant improvement in model accuracy and robustness compared to static parameter tuning methods, highlighting the benefits of dynamic adaptation.

title: A system-level assessment of climate and human-driven pressures on the Gulf of California using fuzzy cognitive maps
abstract: The Gulf of California (GC) is a socio-ecological system exposed to interrelated climate-driven and anthropogenic stressors. Understanding how these pressures propagate is essential for assessing vulnerability and informing environmental management under uncertainty. In this study, we developed a fuzzy cognitive map (FCM) to evaluate the influence of climate change and human activities and to diagnose system-level responses. The model was derived from peer-reviewed literature and refined through literature-based classification and weighting of causal relationships. Simulations were conducted in a virtual laboratory to explore system behavior under two complementary scenarios: (i) a baseline scenario excluding climate change effects, used to isolate the influence of anthropogenic pressures, and (ii) a climate change scenario. Additional minimum- and maximum-weight simulations were performed to evaluate model robustness. The FCM framework integrated environmental, socio-economic, and climatic variables within a structure capable of representing indirect effects, nonlinear relationships, and cascading interactions. Results indicate that rising temperatures, fishing pressure, and coastal pollution act as dominant stressors that intensify ecosystem degradation. Simultaneous deterioration across system components reflects high interconnectedness and limited resilience. Climate change amplifies feedback mechanisms, accelerating trajectories toward more severe ecological and economic outcomes. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the main vulnerability patterns remain consistent across a broad range of weight values. This study provides a diagnosis of the GC under climate and human pressures, highlighting pathways that shape vulnerability. The FCM approach offers insights for identifying key stressors and intervention points and provides a transferable framework for socio-ecological systems facing interrelated climate-driven and anthropogenic pressures.

title: EdgeMem: LLM-Free Agent Memory Construction and Retrieval via Evidence-Preserving Multi-Anchor Hypergraph
abstract: Agent memory allows LLM agents to use earlier interactions when answering new queries. Existing methods often compress interaction histories into summaries or other LLM-generated representations. Repeated generation adds cost and can discard answer-bearing details before the system knows what a future query will require. We propose EdgeMem, an agent-memory method built around a simple principle: preserve original interaction turns and organize them through complementary content, temporal, and episodic cues. EdgeMem realizes this principle with a multi-anchor hypergraph constructed by lightweight local processing. Retrieval directly returns source evidence and reserves LLM use for final answer generation, combining structured access to multi-session histories with faithful retention of the original conversation. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S show strong retrieval and memory-grounded question answering; on LoCoMo, EdgeMem achieves the highest strict-judge score among seven reproduced systems under a shared prompt (61.01 versus 58.70), while construction and retrieval require no generative-LLM calls. Overall, EdgeMem shows that preserving and organizing source evidence provides an effective and efficient foundation for agent memory without generative memory management.

title: Ultrasound-Based Prediction of Cirrhosis Decompensation Using Large-Scale Computer Vision Models
abstract: Decompensation represents a critical transition in the course of cirrhosis, yet clinicians have limited non-invasive tools to reliably predict its onset. In this study, we propose a novel imaging-based approach that leverages large-scale computer vision models to analyze routine abdominal ultrasound images and extract predictive features beyond those captured by traditional laboratory-based risk scores. Ultrasound is widely available, low cost, and suitable for longitudinal surveillance, making it an attractive modality for scalable risk stratification and long-term follow-up. Our framework integrates automated ultrasound data processing with modern deep learning architectures to identify patients at high risk of decompensation prior to the occurrence of clinical deterioration. This non-invasive strategy offers a practical complement to existing clinical scoring systems and may enable earlier, more proactive management of patients with compensated cirrhosis.

title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Post-training VLA policies typically rely on supervised fine-tuning with costly expert demonstrations or reinforcement learning with expensive and potentially unstable real-world exploration. World models offer a promising alternative by evaluating candidate behaviors through imagined futures, yet effective post-training requires more than accurate prediction: imagination must be scheduled where it is useful, bounded within reliable horizons, and translated into trustworthy policy supervision. In robotic manipulation, the value of imagination varies substantially across execution stages, while extended rollouts can accumulate prediction errors and introduce unreliable learning signals. We introduce WISE (World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models), a unified framework that coordinates when and how world-model imagination is used during policy refinement. WISE selectively invokes imagination at interaction-relevant states, performs bounded multi-view rollouts, evaluates candidate futures using progress and completion signals, and uses their relative outcomes to refine actions generated from real interaction contexts. Extensive experiments with both $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$ demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse manipulation tasks while reducing GPU computation time by approximately 80% compared with full imagination. Real-world evaluations further show substantial gains in robustness and generalization under diverse real-world distribution shifts.

title: Markovian Shock-Source Tracing and Multidimensional Asset Roles in Exchange Rates, Gold Futures, and Bitcoin
abstract: This study examines cross-asset connectedness in an international financial network of major exchange rates, gold futures, and Bitcoin. Moving beyond the conventional net transmitter--receiver classification, we characterize asset roles through three complementary dimensions: direct spillover transmission, stationary source-tracing dynamics, and multistep upstream connectivity. Return spillovers are estimated using VAR generalized forecast-error variance decomposition (VAR-GFEVD). The positive pairwise net-spillover structure is then mapped into a row-stochastic Markov kernel whose transitions trace dominant net-spillover sources in the reverse direction of the original transmission edges. A stationary departure flux describes long-run movement in this source-tracing chain, while Viral Centrality is evaluated by the deterministic probability-propagation algorithm of Fink et al. to approximate multistep upstream reach. Empirically, gold futures emerge as the dominant direct net transmitter and the leading stationary source-tracing node, but do not have the largest Viral Centrality. Several exchange-rate nodes classified as direct net receivers have relatively high Viral Centrality, indicating broad conditional access to upstream source nodes. Bitcoin occupies an intermediate role. An auxiliary specification including the U.S. Dollar Index yields qualitatively similar role differentiation. The results show that direct connectedness, stationary source tracing, and approximate multistep upstream reach cannot be inferred from NET spillovers alone. All diffusion interpretations are descriptive and conditional on the estimated network, row normalization, and restart closure.

title: When Do Frozen VLMs Respond to Image-Free Object-Token Edits? An Answer-Key-Free Protocol and What It Reveals
abstract: Answering what-if queries about a scene with a VLM usually means injecting the assumption as text or repainting the scene with a generative model. We instead move the edit to the representation level, before the model input. The image is abstracted into a set of object-level tokens, and the original image never enters the VLM. This design rests on an open question: when do frozen VLMs actually respond to such token edits? We introduce an answer-key-free protocol: no post-edit answer is annotated. It scores edits whose answers are logically determined, and audits itself by reversing each scoreable choice. The protocol reveals three structures. title: DE-Venus: A Data-Efficient RLVR Framework for Large Language Models
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves large language model reasoning, but its practical scaling is constrained by expensive on-policy rollouts and the cost of obtaining reliable targets at scale. Existing methods address sample selection, incomplete supervision, or noisy labels separately, often entangling supervision logic with distributed training and hindering controlled comparison and reuse. We present DE-Venus, a unified framework for data-efficient RLVR that treats supervision as evolving state across data preparation and policy optimization. It organizes this lifecycle into three modules: Active Data Selection allocates training and annotation budgets; Weak Supervision Construction derives learning signals from unlabeled examples; and Training-Time Supervision Refinement filters or corrects unreliable supervision. DE-Venus supports seven representative methods and a data-selection pipeline by expressing method-specific decisions as offline dataset transitions or online transformations of targets, rewards, batches, and advantages while preserving verl's distributed execution contracts. Across public benchmarks and three business scenarios, separate configurations preserve or improve model quality with only 10% of labels or as little as 13% of relevant data; selected business configurations also reduce observed convergence steps by 63%--75%. DE-Venus thus reduces annotation and training costs without sacrificing scalable RL execution.

title: Editable Visual Design
abstract: While diffusion base models such as GPT-Image-2 and Nano-Banana exhibit remarkable visual expressiveness, their end-to-end generation inherently yields flattened bitmaps with error-prone text, precluding layer-wise post-editing. Conversely, code-based visual generation via Coding Agents provides precise layout control and decoupled layers, yet remains constrained by a lack of global aesthetic intuition and the difficulty of coding complex visual assets. To address this, we propose Editable Visual Design, a new paradigm driven by a Coding Agent. We designate the VLM as the ``creative brain'' for requirement comprehension, task planning, and aesthetic judgment, while utilizing the image generation model as an on-demand ``visual world simulator'' to synthesize standalone visual assets. Operating under an ``imagine first, then act'' closed-loop workflow, the agent generates isolated assets, writes native HTML/CSS, and iteratively refines the design against visual rendering feedback. Furthermore, Agent Design Replay faithfully reproduces the creative and reasoning trajectory akin to that of professional human designers. Ultimately, the system delivers editable artifacts with decoupled layers and real text, enabling users to perform intuitive mouse dragging and layout adjustments on a graphical user interface. Validations on posters, infographics, and other scenarios show that this paradigm successfully achieves both refined aesthetics and production-grade editability.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Inflation Forecasting in Nigeria: Interpreting A Multilayer Perceptron Model Using Shap Values
abstract: Inflation forecasting is important for monetary policy, economic planning and decision-making, yet neural-network forecasts can be difficult to interpret because their internal relationships are not directly observable. This study applies SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to interpret a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model developed for forecasting inflation in Nigeria. Monthly macroeconomic data covering 2007–2024 were used, comprising inflation rate, interest rate, exchange rate, oil price and Consumer Price Index (CPI), together with lagged and temporal features used in the MLP. The SHAP analysis was used to explain an individual inflation prediction and identify the direction and relative magnitude of feature contributions. The model prediction examined increased from a baseline of 10.20 to 13.49. The largest positive contributions were associated with the third and first lags of oil price (OP_lag3 and OP_lag1), followed by seasonal and lagged inflation features. CPI variables also contributed positively, whereas exchange-rate and interest-rate variables showed smaller and mixed effects for the prediction examined. The result is consistent with Nigerian evidence that oil-price movements can transmit into domestic inflation, while the importance of lagged inflation supports inflation persistence. The study also demonstrates that SHAP can make an MLP more transparent without treating feature importance as causal evidence. Although the broader thesis found that the MLP did not outperform SARIMA and VAR in out-of-sample accuracy, the SHAP analysis shows that the model learned economically meaningful temporal and macroeconomic information. The study concludes that explainable machine learning can complement conventional inflation forecasting by providing interpretable information about the drivers of individual predictions.

title: Title: Algorithmic Complexity Theory for Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of algorithmic complexity theory to enhance the design and optimization of evolutionary algorithms. Traditional evolutionary algorithm design often relies on heuristics and trial-and-error, lacking a fundamental understanding of the algorithm's inherent complexity. We propose a novel complexity measure – the "exploration efficiency index" – that directly quantifies a search algorithm's capacity to explore the solution space effectively. This index will be integrated into the evolutionary process to guide the selection of individuals and iterations, resulting in improved convergence rates and a more efficient search. The paper details the development and application of this new complexity measure, presenting preliminary results demonstrating its potential to improve the performance of various evolutionary algorithm implementations. We argue that incorporating complexity theory offers a powerful tool for crafting evolutionary algorithms that are not only faster but also more robust and adaptable.

title: Title: Non-Linear Vector Calculus with Adaptive Kernel Selection
abstract: Vector calculus, a foundational tool in mathematics and physics, has historically been constrained by its inherent linearity. This limitation hinders its application to complex, non-linear systems, where traditional methods struggle to provide accurate results. This paper introduces a novel approach to vector calculus – Non-Linear Vector Calculus with Adaptive Kernel Selection – that addresses this bottleneck by dynamically selecting the most appropriate kernel function for each variable within the calculation. The core mechanism involves learning a mapping between the system's dynamics and the kernel function itself, allowing the algorithm to adapt to the specific problem and system characteristics. This leads to improved accuracy and robustness in handling non-linear systems, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses potential future directions.

title: High-Order Group Complexity Model
abstract: The present work introduces a novel high-order group complexity model designed to predict algorithm execution times with improved accuracy and predictability. Traditional complexity analysis often relies on static analysis, limiting its ability to accurately estimate runtime. This model leverages the dynamic properties of high-order groups to provide more precise and insightful complexity estimations. This research focuses on developing a model that adapts to the specific structure of the algorithm being analyzed, leading to a more robust and informative complexity assessment. The core mechanism centers around a refined approach to estimating execution time based on group structure, enabling a significant advancement in computational complexity prediction.

title: 基于动态拓扑的量子计算拓扑验证
abstract: Quantum computation, a revolutionary paradigm in computation, relies heavily on the precise and reliable execution of algorithms. Traditional validation methods, often based on static analysis, struggle to adequately assess the robustness and stability of these quantum circuits. This paper introduces a novel framework, dynamically-oriented quantum topology validation, which leverages quantum entanglement and topological transformations to simulate the evolution of quantum states, thereby providing a robust and adaptable method for validating quantum computational programs. This approach significantly enhances the verification process, offering a dynamic and comprehensive assessment of quantum circuit correctness and stability.

title: 基于动态的概率模型学习的遗传算法
abstract: This paper explores the application of a dynamic probabilistic model to enhance the performance of genetic algorithms. Traditional genetic algorithms often suffer from the limitations of static parameter settings, restricting the search space and hindering optimal solutions. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts the parameters of the probabilistic model during the search process, enabling the algorithm to escape local optima and identify more promising regions of the search space. The core mechanism involves learning a probability distribution that influences the genetic operators, leading to improved search efficiency and higher quality solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and experimental analysis, showing significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to traditional genetic algorithms. The algorithm's ability to adapt to varying data distributions makes it well-suited for complex, real-world problems.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Based on Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed key generation scheme based on quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve fully secure key distribution without prior key exchange. The core concept leverages quantum entanglement between two or more nodes to generate and transmit keys, combined with a quantum key distribution protocol for verification and error correction. Unlike existing quantum key distribution schemes reliant on quantum communication channels, this approach offers a theoretically more secure and potentially efficient method for key sharing. The system utilizes Bell states, polarization measurements, and post-processing techniques to establish a shared key. We outline the key components of the system, including entanglement generation, measurement protocols, error correction, and key distillation. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the security of the scheme against eavesdropping attacks, assuming the validity of quantum mechanics. This work contributes to the ongoing research in quantum cryptography and provides a foundational design for a future generation of secure communication networks.

title: Graph-Based Representation Learning for Natural Language Understanding using Relational Embeddings
abstract: This paper investigates the limitations of traditional word embedding techniques in capturing the intricate relational structures inherent in natural language. We propose a novel approach utilizing graph-based representation learning, specifically employing relational embeddings learned through graph convolutional networks (GCNs). The core idea is to represent language as a graph, where nodes represent words and edges represent semantic relationships derived from various sources like syntactic dependencies and co-occurrence patterns. By learning embeddings that encode these relationships, we aim to create a more nuanced and context-aware representation of word meaning. Our approach demonstrates improved performance in downstream natural language understanding tasks compared to conventional word embedding methods. The key innovation lies in the systematic integration of graph structure with embedding learning, providing a richer representation capable of modeling the complex dependencies that define language.

title: Cognitive Graph Embedding for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) is a crucial task in leveraging the wealth of information stored within knowledge graphs (KGs). Traditional graph embedding methods often treat nodes and edges equally, failing to capture the nuanced relationships and cognitive processes that underpin human understanding of knowledge. This paper proposes a novel cognitive graph embedding framework that integrates attention mechanisms and memory modules to enhance KGC accuracy. The core idea is to model the cognitive aspects of knowledge representation and reasoning by allowing the embedding model to selectively attend to relevant nodes based on their context and retain memories of past interactions. We introduce a new algorithm, Cognitive Graph Embedding (CGE), which incorporates both attention and memory into the embedding process. CGE learns node embeddings that capture both structural information and cognitive biases, resulting in improved performance on KGC benchmarks. The experiments demonstrate that CGE outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in scenarios with sparse or noisy knowledge graphs. The key contributions of this work are the integration of cognitive principles into graph embedding and the development of a practical algorithm for KGC.

title: Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration for Distributed Robot Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed robot control leveraging the power of multi-agent collaboration. Traditional centralized control schemes often struggle with scalability and robustness, particularly in complex environments and dynamic tasks. This research proposes a decentralized control methodology where multiple robots operate autonomously, employing a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework to achieve coordinated task execution. The core innovation lies in the decentralized decision-making process, eliminating the bottleneck of a central controller and enabling robust adaptation to unforeseen circumstances. The system utilizes a distributed MARL algorithm to facilitate communication and cooperation between the robots, allowing them to collectively solve problems that would be intractable for a single robot. The efficacy of the proposed method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, setting the stage for future experimental validation. ---

title: 自适应量子算法的优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization centered on dynamically adjusting quantum algorithm parameters. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, which are inadequate for the inherently variable nature of quantum computation, particularly in the context of large-scale quantum systems. We propose a system that leverages a combination of quantum path optimization and adaptive parameter tuning to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. This research focuses on creating a mechanism that can dynamically adjust quantum algorithm parameters based on the current state of the quantum system, leading to improved performance. The core mechanism involves integrating quantum path optimization with a self-adaptive parameter tuning strategy, enabling the algorithm to self-correct and refine its trajectory. The paper details the proposed system's architecture, demonstrates its effectiveness through theoretical analysis, and provides a preliminary evaluation of its capabilities. The objective is to provide a robust and adaptable framework for optimizing quantum algorithms, addressing a key challenge in the field of quantum computing.

title: Title: Adaptive Probabilistic Graph Embedding for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive probabilistic graph embedding technique designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting the graph structure during training. Traditional graph embedding methods often rely on predefined structures, limiting the model's capacity to represent complex relationships within the data. This work proposes a Bayesian framework where the graph structure is continuously updated based on observed data, allowing the embedding to adapt to the specific characteristics of the training set. The core mechanism involves Bayesian estimation of graph connectivity and node importance, enabling the embedding to learn more robust and nuanced representations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on a diverse range of machine learning tasks, showing significant improvements in model performance, particularly in terms of generalization and robustness to noise.

title: 循环神经网络的自适应正则化机制
abstract: The development of robust and generalizable deep learning models has been a significant challenge in recent years. Traditional regularization techniques often rely on fixed parameters, which can be suboptimal for specific datasets or model architectures. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive regularization mechanism for recurrent neural networks (RNNs) that dynamically adjusts regularization parameters based on both the model's training error and the data distribution. We propose a mechanism that continuously recalibrates the regularization strength, leading to improved generalization performance. This approach addresses the limitations of static regularization methods by providing a flexible and adaptive strategy for model optimization. The core of our work involves a novel error-based and data distribution-aware regularization framework. We evaluate the proposed method on several benchmark RNN tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing model robustness and generalization capabilities.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of nonlinear geometric topology to the prediction of quantum state evolution. We propose a novel model that leverages the inherent properties of non-linear geometric topologies to forecast quantum state trajectories and subsequently optimize quantum device design. The core mechanism focuses on using topology to provide a deeper understanding of quantum behavior, enabling enhanced device design and performance. The model's potential lies in its ability to generate novel design pathways and improve quantum device fidelity. This research offers a new perspective on quantum device optimization, potentially unlocking significant advancements in quantum technology.

The core mechanism centers on exploiting the quantum state's self-correction properties to iteratively refine the reconstructed state. The investigation highlights the algorithm's ability to effectively mitigate errors and enhance fidelity in various quantum state reconstruction scenarios.

title: Title: Geometric Group Theory for Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: The design and optimization of deep learning architectures are profoundly influenced by geometric constraints. This paper investigates the application of geometric group theory as a novel framework to analyze and improve these architectures, aiming to enhance stability and performance. We propose a model where the deep learning architecture is represented as a group of geometric shapes, and geometric transformations are employed to enforce constraints that promote structural integrity and minimize undesirable behavior. This approach offers a more comprehensive and robust method compared to current techniques, which primarily focus on individual layer optimization. This research leverages established geometric principles to create a framework for automated and informed design, ultimately contributing to the development of more reliable and efficient deep learning models.

title: Adaptive Topology-Based Adaptive Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive topology-based machine learning algorithm designed to simulate and predict complex system behavior through dynamic adjustment of topology. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static models, offering limited adaptability. This algorithm leverages adaptive topology to dynamically adjust the structure of the system, enabling the system to adapt to changing conditions. We present a framework for incorporating this topology-based approach, demonstrating its effectiveness in mimicking and predicting complex system dynamics. The core mechanism involves a self-organizing process where the topology evolves based on internal and external factors, resulting in a system that exhibits a degree of resilience and responsiveness. This research focuses on achieving a balance between predictive accuracy and computational efficiency, offering a promising approach to enhancing the capabilities of machine learning models in challenging real-world scenarios.

title: Graph-Based Quantum Computing Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph-based quantum computing framework designed for efficient parallel computation of quantum algorithms. Traditional quantum computing approaches often involve intricate algorithms, but this framework leverages the inherent properties of graphs to significantly enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism centers on transforming quantum algorithms into graph structures, exploiting graph connectivity and node relationships to enable parallel execution. We present a method for optimizing graph representations and utilizing graph traversal techniques to achieve superior performance in various quantum computation tasks. This research aims to provide a robust and scalable solution for parallel quantum algorithm implementation.

abstract: 本書では、データベースに登録されたカフェメニューだけを根拠に商品を推薦する RAG(Retrieval-Augmented Generation)アプリケーションを組み立てる。単に LLM へ質問するのではなく、価格、温冷区分、販売状態、アレルゲンを通常のプログラムと SQL で確実に判定し、その後で文章を生成する。データベースには Turso / libSQL のネイティブベクトル型を使い、会話モデルは OpenAI、OpenAI 互換 API、Anthropic Claude から選べる。外部 API なしで学習できる Fake モデルも用意した。初めて登場する技術用語で読み進めにくくなった場合は、巻末の「初心者向け用語集」を参照してほしい。本文で使う略語や仕組みを、予備知識なしで確認できるようにまとめている。

title: Ensemble clustering: A practical tutorial
abstract: Cluster analysis is an explorative analytical method, serving as a critical tool in psychology, psychiatry, and related fields to map heterogeneous data into meaningful subgroups. Despite their extensive historical use, traditional clustering techniques suffer from a lack of stability, robustness, and generalisability. These issues stem from the inherent difficulties of the clustering optimisation problem as well as the stochastic nature of algorithm optimisers. To address these challenges, we demonstrate the use of methods utilising ensemble learning techniques to combine clustering results from different algorithms, model specifications, and/or sampled sub-datasets to form a single, more reliable consensus of clustering solutions. We detail ensemble clustering principles and variations in base clustering generation models and ensemble methods. More importantly, detailed introductions in existing R libraries and practical examples using R code are provided to guide users in both implementing and optimising ensemble clustering models. As a practical tutorial, we then include simulation studies of real-world data to demonstrate the substantial benefit of ensemble clustering compared with single-run clustering models. The resources presented here will enable researchers to apply advanced clustering techniques to decompose heterogeneous and complex psychological data into stable subgroups.

title: QKD-Assisted Secure Transport Framework for Federated Healthcare Systems: A Software Prototype and Baseline Evaluation
abstract: Decentralised machine learning requires authenticated transport to secure exchanged model updates. To this end, this study presents a healthcare-focused proof of concept integrating a quantum key distribution (QKD) simulation with HKDF-SHA-256, AES-256-GCM, role-based access control, replay detection, and sample-weighted federated averaging (FedAvg), and evaluates it on 42,989 medical records across 1107 synthetic patients. A trusted server decrypted authorised updates before plaintext aggregation. Centralised logistic regression achieved an F1 score of 0.7483, while a five-client FedAvg achieved 0.7333. Encrypted and unencrypted pipelines demonstrated identical model parameters. The simulated QKD protocol produced a mean quantum bit error rate of 0.2486 and successfully aborted all sessions under a full intercept constraint. Under ten independent data splits, the five-client FedAvg achieved mean F1 scores of 0.6973 (IID) and 0.6104 (non-IID). Demonstrating that transport security does not mitigate adversarial machine learning, an authenticated sign-flip attack bypassed AES-256-GCM protection and reduced the mean F1 score to 0.1185. Computationally, the QKD-assisted path averaged 0.386 ms per update compared to 0.486 ms for fresh TLS 1.3 and 0.006 ms for persistent TLS while isolating software execution from hardware constraints. Overall, this study demonstrates a reproducible proof of concept and a practical baseline for a secure machine learning approach for healthcare collaborations.

title: Enhancing E-commerce Chatbot Design with Customer Journey Mapping: Survey and NLP Analysis of User Inquiries
abstract: Despite adoption of chatbots in e-commerce, chatbots struggle to maintain context, provide complete policy guidance, or respond appropriately to post-purchase problems. This study maps user questions as shoppers’ needs at different points in the Customer Journey Map (CJM). A cross-sectional survey collected users’ opinions on expected chatbot interactions in an e-commerce setting. Sixty participants provided responses on which three questions they would ask an e-commerce chatbot during online shopping. Three unsupervised machine-learning approaches were used: Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) topic modeling, K -means clustering, and Lexicon-based analysis. We compared themes and clusters from the Lexicon and K -means methods with the topics generated by LDA. Mapping inquiries to the CJM showed the largest share in Consideration (35%), followed by Decision (30%), Awareness (20%), and Post-Purchase (15%). Overall sentiment of inquiries was observed to be predominantly neutral, Awareness questions had a largely positive tone, and Post-Purchase questions had a largely negative tone.
